basic_information.official_title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A REVOLVING FUND FOR THE PAYMENT OF SALARIES, COMPENSATION, AND EMOLUMENTS OF WORKERS AND PERSONNEL OF NATIONALLY FUNDED PROGRAMS DEPLOYED IN THE BANGSAMORO AUTONOMOUS REGION IN MUSLIM MINDANAO, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
signed_by: Prof. Raby B. Angkal, Secretary General
basic_information.effectivity: 15 days after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation

citizen_summary.what_is_this_about: Creates a ₱1 billion standby fund so workers on nationally-funded programmes in the region get paid on time even when the national government's money arrives late.
citizen_summary.why_was_it_proposed: Workers deployed under national programmes but supervised by Bangsamoro ministries were going unpaid when national funds were delayed in transfer or downloading. The act builds a bridge.
citizen_summary.what_will_change: When national funds are late, the Bangsamoro ministry can draw on the Fund to pay salaries, compensation and emoluments — and the Fund is reimbursed once the national agency finally transfers the money.
who_will_be_affected: Workers and personnel on nationally-funded programmes in the region, supervised by Bangsamoro ministries
Bangsamoro ministries, agencies and offices implementing those programmes
The Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management, which administers the Fund
citizen_summary.when_will_it_take_effect: In force since 2023 — 15 days after publication.

what_this_means_for_you.in_short: NOW LAW. If you work on a nationally-funded programme run by a Bangsamoro ministry and the national money is late, there is a ₱1 billion fund to pay you on time. It gets repaid when the national funds arrive.
in_practice: ₱1,000,000,000 revolving fund, charged against the Contingent Fund
Covers salaries, compensation and emoluments of nationally-funded workers directly supervised by BARMM ministries, agencies or offices
Used specifically when there is delay in the transfer or downloading of funds by national government agencies
Released by the Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management on request by the concerned ministry
Reimbursed to the Fund immediately once the national agency transfers the corresponding funds
A quarterly report on releases, obligations and disbursements goes to Parliament through the Speaker

for_specific_groups.Workers on national programmes: You are the reason the Fund exists — it is there so a delay in Manila does not become a missed payday in the region.
for_specific_groups.Bangsamoro ministries: You request a release from the Fund and must still do what is required to get the national funds downloaded.
for_specific_groups.Parliament: Quarterly reports on releases, obligations and disbursements, submitted through the Speaker.

what_this_means_for_you.where_this_applies: Nationally-funded programmes implemented in the BARMM under Bangsamoro ministry supervision.
what_this_means_for_you.when_you_will_feel_it: In force since 2023 — when national funds are delayed.
what_you_can_do: If your salary on a nationally-funded programme is delayed, ask the supervising Bangsamoro ministry whether it has requested a release from the Revolving Fund
Ask for the quarterly utilisation report, which goes to Parliament through the Speaker
watch_out_for: The Fund covers delay, not liability — Section 5 says nothing in the act makes the Bangsamoro Government responsible for national government obligations.
It pays only workers directly supervised by BARMM ministries, agencies or offices.
The Fund is hard to wind up: it survives programme discontinuance and only dissolves after two fiscal years with no requests.
No penalty attaches if a ministry fails to request a release.

key_terms_explained.Revolving fund: A standing pot that is drawn down and then replenished, rather than spent once.
key_terms_explained.Downloading of funds: The transfer of money from a national agency to a regional or local implementer.
key_terms_explained.Emoluments: Payments for holding a post, beyond basic salary.
key_terms_explained.Contingent Fund: The budget reserve the ₱1 billion is charged against.
key_terms_explained.Reversion: Returning unused money to the Treasury — here only after two fiscal years without a request.

what_this_means_for_you.status_note: Passed Shawwal 26, 1444 / 17 May 2023, approved by the Chief Minister on 22 May 2023.

benefits.headline: ₱1 billion standing behind the paycheques of workers on nationally-funded programmes.

direct_benefits.benefit: Timely payment of salaries, compensation and emoluments despite national funding delays
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Nationally-funded workers and personnel supervised by BARMM ministries
direct_benefits.how_to_access: The supervising ministry requests a release from the MFBM

direct_benefits.benefit: A quarterly public account of the Fund's use
direct_benefits.who_gets_it: Parliament and, through it, the public
direct_benefits.how_to_access: MFBM report to Parliament through the Speaker

indirect_benefits: Continuity of national programme delivery in the region
Automatic reimbursement once national funds arrive, so the Fund is not depleted
limitations: Covers only workers directly supervised by BARMM ministries, agencies or offices.
Does not transfer national government liability to the region.
No sanction if a ministry does not request a release.

for_ministries: Do what is required to secure the downloading of funds from the National Government
Request releases from the Fund where there is delay
Reimburse the Fund once national funds are transferred

what_is_prohibited: The act defines no prohibited acts and creates no offences. The Fund may be released only for the purpose specified.

penalties.for_citizens: None. The act creates no offence, fine or imprisonment.

where_to_complain.first_stop: The Bangsamoro ministry, agency or office supervising your programme
where_to_complain.oversight: Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management, which administers the Fund; and the Parliament's Committee on Finance, Budget and Management
where_to_complain.note: The act creates no complaints procedure, but the quarterly report is a document a citizen can ask for.

everyday_scenarios: A health worker on a nationally-funded programme supervised by the regional health ministry is not paid because the national transfer is late. The ministry can request a release from the Revolving Fund so the salary is paid on time, and the Fund is repaid when the national money arrives.
A programme ends and hiring stops. The Fund is not automatically dissolved — it survives, and reverts to the Treasury only after two fiscal years in which no ministry has requested anything from it.

key_provisions: Section 1 — Short title: the “Bangsamoro Revolving Fund Act of 2023”.

Section 2 — Policy: the Bangsamoro Government shall afford workers in the region full protection and promotion of their general welfare, and shall protect the interests of its workers and personnel — including those deployed under programmes funded by the National Government — by developing a mechanism ensuring timely payment of authorised salaries, compensation and emoluments for services rendered.

Section 3 — Establishes the Bangsamoro Revolving Fund for nationally-funded programmes, for the payment of salaries, compensation and emoluments of nationally-funded workers and personnel directly supervised by BARMM ministries, agencies or offices implementing nationally-funded programmes. The Fund ensures timely payment in case of delay in the transfer or downloading of funds by the national government agencies concerned.

Section 4 — The Fund is administered and managed by the Ministry of Finance, and Budget and Management under its cash management and disbursement system, subject to government accounting and auditing rules. It is released only for the specified purpose upon request by the concerned ministry, agency or office. The MFBM must ensure the availability of the requested amount immediately after effectivity, and must provide a mechanism for reimbursing the Fund immediately once the national agency has transferred or downloaded the corresponding funds.

Section 5 — The ministries concerned must fulfil their roles for the downloading of funds from the National Government. Nothing in the act shall be construed as the Bangsamoro Government assuming the responsibilities of the National Government for the salaries, compensation and emoluments of nationally funded programmes.

Section 6 — The Fund is not automatically dissolved on discontinuance of nationally-funded programmes, on the lapse of its appropriation, or on the cessation of hiring or renewal of deployed workers. It is dissolved and reverted to the Bangsamoro Treasury only when the ministries authorised to draw from it have stopped submitting requests for at least two fiscal years. Reversion is reported by the MFBM to the Chief Minister in the Parliament through the Committee on Finance, Budget and Management.
Section 7 — Appropriates ₱1,000,000,000 as the revolving fund, chargeable against the Contingent Fund.
Section 8 — The MFBM shall issue implementing rules governing request, utilisation and disbursement within 1 month after complete publication.
Section 9 — An official quarterly report on releases, obligations and disbursements shall be submitted by the MFBM to Parliament through the Speaker, in printed or electronic form.
Section 12 — Takes effect 15 days after publication in a newspaper of regional circulation.

citizen_questions.q: Does the region end up paying for national obligations?
citizen_questions.a: No. Section 5 says nothing in the act shall be construed as the Bangsamoro Government assuming the National Government's responsibilities. The Fund is reimbursed once the national agency transfers the money.
₱1 billion, charged against the Contingent Fund, replenished as reimbursements come in.

citizen_questions.a: Yes. Section 9 requires a quarterly report on releases, obligations and disbursements to Parliament through the Speaker.
